newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises after sharp rebound.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises after sharp rebound.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar on Wednesday recovering from early losses that followed the U.S. currency's decline in overseas markets, dealers said.

"The session opened with another decline of the shekel and the dollar rose above 3.2 shekels. The rise of the dollar pushed the basket downwards and the central bank had to intervene in the market (buying dollars) on a relatively large scale," said one dealer.
"By midday the shekel rose sharply following the dollar's correction against the mark in Europe," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3120 shekels against 3.3190 shekels on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6255 shekels against 3.6253 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7119 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7466 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0174 shekels against 2.0062 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3310 shekels.
